title: A Noetherian domain is N-1 from a normal principal open and N-1 maximal localizations
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with fraction field $K$. If some nonzero $f\in A$ has normal localization $A_f$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, then the integral closure of $A$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], i.e. $A$ is N-1.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), lines 45482-45539, implication (1)+(2) => N-1

proof.text: Notation. Let $A'\subseteq K$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], a subring of $K$ containing $A$. Since $A_f$ is an integral domain (a subring of $K$, $f\neq0$) and a normal ring, it is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] (its last sentence); its fraction field is $K$ (every $a/b\in K$ is $(a/1)/(b/1)$ with $a/1,b/1\in A_f$). Let $\mathcal C$ be the set of subrings $B\subseteq K$ with $A\subseteq B\subseteq A'$ which are finitely generated $A$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Every $B\in\mathcal C$ is an integral domain with fraction field $K$ (as $A\subseteq B\subseteq K$), is integral over $A$ (as $B\subseteq A'$), and is a Noetherian ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] since $A$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, first paragraph ('Suppose that R ⊂ R' ⊂ K is a finite extension of R contained in K')

proof.text: For $B\in\mathcal C$, $B_f=A_f$ inside $K$. Indeed, apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] to the inclusion $A\to B$ and $S=\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$: the integral closure of $A$ in $B$ is $B$ (all of $B$ is integral over $A$), so every element of $B_f=S^{-1}B$ is integral over $A_f$. Both are subrings of $K$ ($B_f=\{b/f^n\}$, the localization of a subring of the field $K$ at nonzero elements), $A_f\subseteq B_f\subseteq K$, and $A_f$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K$ (step 1), i.e. integrally closed in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; hence $B_f\subseteq A_f$, so $B_f=A_f$. In particular $B_f$ is a normal domain, and $f\neq0$ in $B$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, first paragraph: 'Note that R_f = R'_f since R_f is already normal'

proof.text: Definition of $Z_B$. For $B\in\mathcal C$, $B$ is a Noetherian domain with $B_f$ a normal domain (steps 1, 2), so by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-locus-open] the set $U_B=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B: B_{\mathfrak q}\text{ normal domain}\}$ is open and its complement $E_B$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}B$. As $B$ is integral over $A$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\mathfrak q\mapsto\mathfrak q\cap A$, is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map]; so $Z_B:=\{\mathfrak q\cap A:\mathfrak q\in E_B\}$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. By construction, a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ is not in $Z_B$ if and only if $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ with $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, first paragraph: 'Hence by Lemma 0332 the set of primes p' with R'_{p'} non-normal is closed in Spec(R'). Since Spec(R') -> Spec(R) is closed the image of this set is closed in Spec(R). For such a ring R' denote Z_{R'} this image.'

proof.text: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$ there is $B\in\mathcal C$ with $\mathfrak m\notin Z_B$. Let $S=A\setminus\mathfrak m$. The fraction field of $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is $K$, and by hypothesis $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]: the integral closure $(A_{\mathfrak m})'$ of $A_{\mathfrak m}$ in $K$ is generated as an $A_{\mathfrak m}$-module by finitely many $y_1,\dots,y_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] to $A\to K$ and $S$: since $S^{-1}K=K$ (the elements of $S$ are nonzero, hence units in $K$), $(A_{\mathfrak m})'=S^{-1}A'=\{x/s:x\in A',s\in S\}\subseteq K$. Write $y_j=x_j/s_j$ with $x_j\in A'$, $s_j\in S$, and put $B=A[x_1,\dots,x_n]\subseteq A'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators], $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, so $B\in\mathcal C$. Its localization $S^{-1}B=A_{\mathfrak m}[x_1,\dots,x_n]\subseteq K$ lies in $S^{-1}A'=(A_{\mathfrak m})'$ and contains each $y_j=x_j\cdot(1/s_j)$, hence contains the $A_{\mathfrak m}$-module they generate: $S^{-1}B=(A_{\mathfrak m})'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal] (with $P=A_{\mathfrak m}$, $L=K$), $(A_{\mathfrak m})'$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K$. Now let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime with $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$. Then $\mathfrak q\cap S=\emptyset$, so $S\subseteq B\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $B_{\mathfrak q}$ (as a subring of $K$, $\{b/t:t\in B\setminus\mathfrak q\}$) is the localization of $S^{-1}B=(A_{\mathfrak m})'$ at the multiplicative subset of the elements $t/s$, $t\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$, $s\in S$, which does not contain $0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain. Hence $\mathfrak m\notin Z_B$ (step 3).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, second paragraph ('Pick a maximal ideal m ⊂ R ... With this choice it is clear that m ∉ Z_{R'}')

proof.text: Finitely many $B_i$ suffice. For each maximal $\mathfrak m$ choose $B_{\mathfrak m}$ as in step 4; $W_{\mathfrak m}=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus Z_{B_{\mathfrak m}}$ is open (step 3) and contains $\mathfrak m$. These opens cover $\operatorname{Spec}A$: a prime $\mathfrak p$ lies in some maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]; if $\mathfrak p\in Z_{B_{\mathfrak m}}$, then, $Z_{B_{\mathfrak m}}$ being closed and the closure of $\{\mathfrak p\}$ in the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum] being $V(\mathfrak p)\ni\mathfrak m$, we would get $\mathfrak m\in Z_{B_{\mathfrak m}}$, a contradiction; so $\mathfrak p\in W_{\mathfrak m}$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], finitely many $W_{\mathfrak m_1},\dots,W_{\mathfrak m_r}$ cover it; with $B_i=B_{\mathfrak m_i}\in\mathcal C$ this means $Z_{B_1}\cap\dots\cap Z_{B_r}=\emptyset$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, third paragraph: 'As Spec(R) is quasi-compact, the above shows that we can find a finite collection R ⊂ R'_i ⊂ K such that ∩ Z_{R'_i} = ∅'

proof.text: The compositum. Let $B\subseteq K$ be the subring generated by $B_1,\dots,B_r$. Each $B_i$ is generated as an $A$-module, a fortiori as an $A$-algebra, by finitely many elements of $A'$; together these finitely many elements generate $B$ as an $A$-algebra and are integral over $A$, so $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators], and $B\subseteq A'$ since $A'$ is a subring. Thus $B\in\mathcal C$ and $B_i\subseteq B$ for all $i$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, third paragraph: 'Let R' be the subring of K generated by all of these. It is finite over R.'

proof.text: $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$. Let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$; by step 5 there is $i$ with $\mathfrak p\notin Z_{B_i}$. The prime $\mathfrak q_i=\mathfrak q\cap B_i$ of $B_i$ satisfies $\mathfrak q_i\cap A=\mathfrak p$, so $(B_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is a normal domain (step 3), with fraction field $K$. Let $T=B_i\setminus\mathfrak q_i$. Every element of $B$ is integral over $A$, hence over $B_i\supseteq A$ (the same monic equation), so the integral closure of $B_i$ in $B$ is $B$ and by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] (for $B_i\to B$ and $T$) every element of $T^{-1}B$ is integral over $T^{-1}B_i=(B_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}$. As $(B_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}\subseteq T^{-1}B\subseteq K$ and $(B_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is integrally closed in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $T^{-1}B=(B_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is a normal domain. Since $T\subseteq B\setminus\mathfrak q$, $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization of $T^{-1}B$ at the multiplicative subset $\{b/t: b\in B\setminus\mathfrak q,\ t\in T\}$, which does not contain $0$, so $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. (The source writes this as $R'_{\mathfrak p'}=(R'_i)_{\mathfrak p'_i}$; only normality of $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is used.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, third paragraph: 'Also Z_{R'} = ∅. Namely, every prime p' lies over a prime p'_i such that (R'_i)_{p'_i} is normal. This implies that R'_{p'} = (R'_i)_{p'_i} is normal too.'

proof.text: Conclusion. By step 7, $B_{\mathfrak n}$ is a normal domain for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of the domain $B$, so $B$ is a normal domain [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal], i.e. integrally closed in its fraction field $K$. Every $x\in A'$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A\subseteq B$, hence $x\in B$; so $A'\subseteq B\subseteq A'$ and $A'=B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module: $A$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].
